Photograph: Clemens Bilan/EPA Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) Anti-AfD protests sweep Germany as far right closes in on two more states Alarm that Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania may fall next after party’s Saxony-Anhalt election victory ‘It breaks my heart’: victory sparks dismay Europe live – latest updates Deborah Cole in Berlin Tue 8 Sep 2026 08.54 EDT Last modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 11.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Thousands of Germans have staged protests against the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) after the party’s watershed victory in a state election, warning it posed a danger in two more polls this month. Demonstrators at Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate held a peaceful pro-democracy rally denouncing the anti-immigrant, pro-Russian AfD, which has called for mass deportations of asylum seekers and a rollback of state support for renewable energy and public broadcasting. The party captured its best-ever state result in the former communist eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, with clear momentum heading into regional elections in the capital and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, on the Baltic coast, on 20 September. Police reported 5,000 protesters, while organisers said they drew more than 14,000 people in a campaign to mobilise voters against the AfD. Posters in the crowd read: “Fascism is no alternative”, “Stop the Nazi AfD: end racism and cuts to social services” and “History has its eyes on us”. With less than two weeks to election day, demonstrators at the Berlin rally cautioned against resignation and cynicism after Sunday’s shock result. The AfD’s nearly 44% vote in Saxony-Anhalt, the best for a nativist party since the Nazi period , is a “disgrace that makes you furious and stunned”, Jens-Christian Wagner, the director of the memorial at the former Nazi concentration camp Buchenwald, said from the stage. View image in fullscreen Protesters throng the roads around the Brandenburg Gate, Berlin, on Monday after the AfD victory. Photograph: Dpa Picture Alliance/Alamy Wagner sounded the alarm that the AfD, although it fell just short of an absolute majority, was on the brink of taking power in Saxony-Anhalt, a first for the far right since the second world war. That “should not be accepted in silence”, he said. Max Schneller, 17, a member of the far-left Linke, from Saxony-Anhalt, said activists in the state would fight any attempts by an AfD government to target minorities. “We will not start categorising our neighbours according to their origin, religion or skin colour – we are too humane to hate,” he said to loud applause. The AfD is three votes short of the support necessary to form a government under its candidate, the media-savvy firebrand Ulrich Siegmund, who hopes to peel off dissenters from the remaining parties willing to play kingmaker. Germany’s domestic intelligence agency has since 2023 listed the state chapter of the party as rightwing extremist, saying it poses a threat to democratic norms. Hundreds of anti-AfD protesters also gathered in Potsdam, near Berlin, with rallies also organised in Münster, Göttingen, Dresden, Aachen, Bamberg, Darmstadt, and Halberstadt, in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD captured nearly half the votes, local media reported. View image in fullscreen A protester in Berlin on Monday. Photograph: Maryam Majd/Reuters In Halle, the region’s second largest city, leftist groups and civil society organisations have been staging a protest camp since election day. The AfD is leading in voter intent polls in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania , with about 35%. However, the centre-left Social Democratic party (SPD) of the state premier, Manuela Schwesig, mounted a remarkable comeback over the summer and is now scoring above 30%. In Berlin, one of Germany’s 16 federal states, the picture is more mixed, with several parties jockeying for first place . It is governed by a coalition of conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) and the SPD. The CDU, the party of chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose record unpopularity is reported to have weighed heavily with voters in Saxony-Anhalt , holds a wafer-thin lead in the capital, with about 20%. Hot on its heels is the Linke, which has focused on soaring housing costs in its campaign, and the AfD, followed by the SPD and the ecologist Greens, both polling in the mid-teens. Merz has vowed to stay in office and fight for a signature package of painful reforms, arguing the only way to defeat the AfD is to get Europe’s top economy moving again and repair its creaking social welfare system. However, the SPD, his junior coalition partner, has indicated its willingness to backtrack on some of the most unpopular measures to shore up support for the embattled government. Analysts say the dispute could further destabilise the shaky coalition. China and North Korea open New Yalu River Bridge after 12-year delay Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 15/10/2026 - 10:13 GMT+2 China and North Korea opened a new four-lane road bridge on Thursday, 15 October, ending a 12-year delay and creating a major new route for cross-border trade. … More The 3,026-metre, four-lane New Yalu River Bridge links the Chinese border city of Dandong with Sinuiju in North Korea . Hundreds of people gathered in Dandong on Thursday to watch as lorries began crossing in both directions , some decorated with Chinese and North Korean flags and flowers. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Completed in 2014 , the bridge had stood unused for 12 years because connecting roads and customs facilities on the North Korean side were not finished. Its official opening marks a significant step in efforts to revive trade between the two countries after years of strained relations and pandemic-era border restrictions . The crossing is expected to ease freight transport and reduce reliance on the ageing Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge nearby, which has carried much of the cross-border traffic since 1943 . Lim Eul-chul, a North Korea expert at Kyungnam University, estimated that the new crossing could triple or quadruple cargo traffic, particularly shipments of heavy machinery and construction materials. China remains North Korea's largest trading partner and a crucial economic ally . Residents in Dandong hope the new link will bring more business and improve living standards across the border, although North Korea has yet to resume issuing tourist visas to Chinese visitors. August 27, 2026 OPINION Thailand makes a play for digital nomads May 11, 2026 OPINION Taxing tourism: A lesson we keep relearning May 6, 2026 SUBSCRIBE NEWS AIRLINES DESTINATIONS EUROPE Facebook Twitter Email Print Copy URL BANGKOK, 12 October 2026: LOT Polish Airlines reintroduced direct scheduled flights from Warsaw, Poland, to Bangkok on 7 October after a 26-year gap, serving cities in Southeast Asia. The inaugural flight lasting 10 hours and 20 minutes was operated by a Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft. Bangkok is the latest long-haul Asian destination in LOT Polish Airlines’ route network flying from its home base at Warsaw’s Chopin Airport. For years, Bangkok has remained one of Asia’s most attractive and promising destinations and has been served by seasonal ad hoc charter flights since the airline ended scheduled flights in 2000. The launch of direct flights from Warsaw marks another step in strengthening LOT’s presence in Southeast Asia, offering a new connection that will help deepen ties between Poland and Thailand. LO65 departs Warsaw for Bangkok on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Saturdays at 1545 Photo credit: LOT Polish. LO66 from Bangkok to Warsaw will depart on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Sundays at 0905. With the start of the winter season on 26 October, flights will increase to five times a week, and from 2 November, flights to Bangkok will operate six times a week (no flight on Fridays). During this period, the departure time from Warsaw will also change from 1545 to 1445. Return flights to Warsaw will depart daily at 0905, except on Saturdays. For the summer season — 28 March to 28 October 2027 — the airline will maintain three flights weekly to the Thai capital. The return of flights to Bangkok marks a new chapter in this route’s history, which dates back to 1977, when LOT Polish Airlines launched its first scheduled service to the Far East, connecting Warsaw with Bangkok. Initially, flights included stopovers, with the Warsaw–Dubai–Mumbai–Bangkok route operated using Ilyushin Il-62 aircraft. As the fleet expanded and LOT introduced Boeing 767 aircraft, it launched direct flights to Thailand but suspended regular service from Warsaw in March 2000 to allow route expansion in North America. The accident occurred when one train, travelling at high speed, ploughed into the back of another that was stationary on the Madrid-Seville line, near the small town of Urda, about 40 miles from Toledo. It was the worst rail tragedy in Spain since 2013. Twenty-eight people remain in hospital. "The tragic accident in Urda has left our families, our towns and our society with a pain that is difficult to accept," Archbishop Cerro Chaves told those present. Representatives of those killed carried lit candles to the front of the cathedral and placed them next to the main altar. The first reading of the service was by Ana BenÃ­tez, sister of David BenÃ­tez, a 38-year-old father-of-two who died. The king and queen were met with applause by bystanders as they entered the cathedral and at the end of the service, after Catholic Mass, they spoke to relatives of the victims. Senior politicians also attended the service, including the leader of the opposition People's Party, Alberto NÃºÃ±ez FeijÃ³o, the president of the Castilla-La Mancha region, Emiliano GarcÃ­a-Page, and Transport and Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo. Cuerpo took on the transport portfolio following the resignation last week of Ãscar Puente from the post. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The Archbishop of Toledo officiated the memorial service Puente had come under mounting pressure following the crash, Spain's second major rail tragedy this year after 46 people died in a collision on the same high-speed line in January. Some local people from the town of Adamuz in Andalusia, where that accident happened, as well as residents of Urda, were present for the memorial service. The investigation into the recent accident is still in progress. Puente suggested that human error combined with a glitch in the safety system may have been the cause. The tragedy happened a month before the 29 November general election and is seen as likely to hurt Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez's attempts to secure re-election. The ceremony took place on the same day as a nationwide strike by train drivers, who are demanding greater safety on the rail network. Rail services were also expected to be affected across the country on Wednesday due to a general strike, led by housing activists calling for urgent measures to control rental costs.
